While Applause doesn't embed attachments for this bug, here are the links for quick view:
https://platform.applause.com/services/links/v1/external/76cb545b82d98da75e1a03fc7282cd3577d8c6bf3251d18752241c0390651f70

> ⚠️ **Preliminary analysis (low confidence)**: treat this as a starting point, not a conclusion.

I think the App hides the card on purpose because of the state the card gets after archiving. The workspace Expensify Card page reads cards through [`filterInactiveCardsForWorkspace`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/f8bb9886c921b49056f054ead83d0f90d6257502/src/pages/workspace/expensifyCard/WorkspaceExpensifyCardPage.tsx#L40). That filter always drops cards in state `5` (`STATE_DEACTIVATED`) or `6` (`CLOSED`). It keeps state `7` (`STATE_SUSPENDED`), which shows as "Inactive" ([`src/libs/CardUtils.ts:1528-1533`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/f8bb9886c921b49056f054ead83d0f90d6257502/src/libs/CardUtils.ts#L1528-L1533)). If archiving moves the card to state `5` or `6`, the list is empty, which matches the video.

The App doesn't change any card data when it archives. [`archivePolicy`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/f8bb9886c921b49056f054ead83d0f90d6257502/src/libs/actions/Policy/Policy.ts#L743-L785) only sets `archivedDate` optimistically. The card's state after archiving comes from the server, so this appears to be a backend/internal issue. A separate internal investigation is needed.

I couldn't verify this because I don't have log access in this run. I also couldn't set up an Expensify Card on a test account. To confirm, check the card's `state` in the Onyx data for `cards_<fundID>_Expensify Card` after archiving.

<details>
<summary>Investigation details</summary>

**What the archive flow promises:** The confirmation text says archiving "will set all Expensify Card limits to $0" ([`src/languages/en.ts:5003`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/f8bb9886c921b49056f054ead83d0f90d6257502/src/languages/en.ts#L5003)). It doesn't say cards are deactivated. An admin-zeroed card is meant to stay visible in state `7`.

**Why state `5` is hidden:** [Allow $0 as valid card limit when editing Expensify Card](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/90540) (`Expensify/App#90540`) stopped showing `STATE_DEACTIVATED` cards because the server rejects limit updates for them with a 403. A unit test locks this in. That change happened before archiving existed. Archiving came in with [feat: Replace Delete with Archive behind the archivePolicies beta](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/98029) (`Expensify/App#98029`), merged 2026-10-06.

**Ruled out in App code:**
- The page doesn't skip the data request for archived workspaces. `OpenPolicyExpensifyCardsPage` always runs ([`WorkspaceExpensifyCardPage.tsx:43-52`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/f8bb9886c921b49056f054ead83d0f90d6257502/src/pages/workspace/expensifyCard/WorkspaceExpensifyCardPage.tsx#L43-L52)).
- The page isn't blocked for archived workspaces. It opens read-only, and only the list is empty.

**Other possible cause:** The list page also drops cards whose cardholder isn't in `policy.employeeList` ([`WorkspaceExpensifyCardListPage.tsx:144-147`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/f8bb9886c921b49056f054ead83d0f90d6257502/src/pages/workspace/expensifyCard/WorkspaceExpensifyCardListPage.tsx#L144-L147)). If the archived workspace's data arrives without that member, or the server doesn't return the card at all, you'd see the same empty list.

**Possible fixes, depending on what the server sends:**
- Card is in state `5` or `6`: the server should use state `7` with a $0 limit, which matches the archive copy. Or the App could list state `5` cards read-only on archived workspaces.
- Card is in state `7`: the card is missing from the data. This needs the internal investigation.

**Related issues:** none found that match this bug.

</details>

---
**Next Steps:** Reply with `@MelvinBot <your feedback>` to refine this analysis.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
When navigating to an archived workspace (Settings -> Workspaces -> Filters: Archived -> [Workspace] -> Expensify Card), no Expensify Cards are displayed and an empty view is shown, instead of rendering the workspace's cards in an inactive, read-only state with limit $0.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
When an Expensify workspace is archived, its issued Expensify cards are automatically transitioned to deactivated state (`CONST.EXPENSIFY_CARD.STATE.STATE_DEACTIVATED`).

Two root causes prevent cards from rendering in archived workspaces:
1. Card Filtering in `WorkspaceExpensifyCardPage`:
The page uses `filterInactiveCardsForWorkspace`, which delegates to `filterAllInactiveCards` and `isActiveCard` in `CardUtils.ts`. `isActiveCard` unconditionally drops cards where `card.state === STATE_DEACTIVATED`. Consequently, all cards belonging to an archived workspace are filtered out from `cardsList`, causing the page to display `EmptyCardView`.
2. Missing Status Label for Deactivated Cards in `CardUtils`:
`getTranslationKeyForCardStatus` only translates `STATE_NOT_ISSUED`, `NOT_ACTIVATED`, `OPEN`, and `STATE_SUSPENDED`. It lacks a case for `STATE_DEACTIVATED`. Even if the card is retained in the list, its status column renders empty rather than showing the expected "Inactive" badge.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. In `CardUtils.ts`:
- Extend `isActiveCard` and `filterAllInactiveCards` to accept an `isArchivedWorkspace` flag (default `false`). When `isArchivedWorkspace` is true, include cards in `STATE_DEACTIVATED`. This ensures active workspaces continue filtering out deactivated cards to prevent edit/update conflicts (preserving PR #90540), while archived workspaces preserve deactivated cards for historical inspection.
- In `getTranslationKeyForCardStatus`, map `CONST.EXPENSIFY_CARD.STATE.STATE_DEACTIVATED` to `'workspace.expensifyCard.statusInactive'`.
2. In `WorkspaceExpensifyCardPage.tsx`:
- Detect if the workspace policy is archived via `isArchivedPolicy(policy)`.
- Pass the archived flag into `filterAllInactiveCards` so deactivated cards remain visible in the table.
3. In `DynamicWorkspaceExpensifyCardDetailsPage.tsx`:
- Pass `isArchivedPolicy(policy)` when fetching cards via `getAllCardsForWorkspace` so navigating to card details in an archived workspace loads the card.
4. Read-Only Protection:
- For archived workspaces, `usePolicyFeatureWriteAccess` already sets `canWrite: false`, disabling card issuance and limit editing actions, keeping the view strictly read-only.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
- Unconditionally displaying deactivated cards in all workspaces: This would cause regressions in active workspaces where admins might attempt to modify limits on deactivated cards, triggering 403 API errors.
- Storing a separate archived card list in Onyx: Overcomplicates state management when a simple boolean policy-archived flag in the existing filter selector achieves complete correctness.

### What specific scenarios should we cover in automated tests?
In `tests/unit/CardUtilsTest.ts`:
- Verify `filterAllInactiveCards` with `isArchivedWorkspace: true` retains cards with `state: STATE_DEACTIVATED`.
- Verify `filterAllInactiveCards` with `isArchivedWorkspace: false` excludes cards with `state: STATE_DEACTIVATED`.
- Verify `getTranslationKeyForCardStatus` returns `'workspace.expensifyCard.statusInactive'` for `STATE_DEACTIVATED`.
In `WorkspaceExpensifyCardPageTest.tsx`:
- Verify that for an archived policy, the Expensify cards table renders deactivated cards with the "Inactive" status badge.
